newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares seen falling further on US declines.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares seen falling further on US declines.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower on Thursday, hit by Wall Street declines, with dealers seeing another negative day ahead up to the weekend.

"The New Year got off to a bad start because of America after ending 1996 at a record high index level, but Danish stock recovered a little later on in the day, reducing some of the earlier losses. Tomorrow looks negative again," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 1.45 point or 1.07 percent down at 134.68, having dropped 2.01 point at its lowest point in the early morning before rallying. The KFX March future was untraded at 135.70.
Dealers saw Wall Street determining Friday's market trends, but generally expected more falls.

Novo Nordisk lost 23 crowns to finish at 532, under pressure because of the weaker dollar and the possibility of a massive sell off of staff shares, while Tele Danmark closed four crowns lower at 321.
One of the few KFX papers to start off the new year with a rise was Copenhagen Airports, which ended the day 12 crowns up at 612.
Overall turnover for the day was 1.011 billion crowns. --Chris Follett, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969650
